A different method of awarding grades is proposed for the examinations. This new grading
system will use three grades represented by the letters A, B, and C.
Grades A, B, or C will be calculated as follows:
y The average mark for all students is calculated.
y Grade A is awarded if an individual student’s marks are more than 20 marks above the
average mark for all students.
y Grade B is awarded if an individual student’s marks are within 20 marks of the average
mark for all students.
y Grade C is awarded if an individual student’s marks are more than 20 marks below the
average mark for all students.
For example, if the average mark for all students is 49.5:
y Grade A is awarded if a student’s marks are greater than 69.5.
y Grade B is awarded if a student’s marks are in the range from 29.5 to 69.5 inclusive.
y Grade C is awarded if a student’s marks are less than 29.5.
